page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c4d server family. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs and 7.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-core ratio of 1.75 GB per vCPU, aligning with compute-focused workloads that require dedicated processing power without a large memory footprint.

This instance type does not include bundled local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external network-attached block storage. Additionally, the c4d-highcpu-4 does not feature any integrated graphics processing units and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable compute performance for CPU-bound tasks, avoiding the performance degradation associated with shared-core or burstable instances. The low memory-to-CPU ratio makes it a resource-dense option for workloads that do not require extensive RAM, such as web serving, batch processing, and lightweight computational tasks.
